# Turn messy phone photos into a family album with Google Photos AI


Imagine opening your phone and finding every photo of your kids, your partner, or your dog already gathered in one album — no endless scrolling, no guessing. Google Photos can group your pictures by the faces in them (Google calls this **Face Groups**), and a **live album** keeps adding new photos of the people you choose, all by itself.

---

## Before you start
- A phone or tablet with the **Google Photos app** (Android or iPhone), signed in with your free Google account.
- Some family photos already in Google Photos.
- Face Groups isn't available in every country. If you can't find it, see Common mistakes below.
- Rough total time: **7–10 minutes**.

The button names below come from Google's own Google Photos Help for Android. On an iPhone they are the same or very close.

---

## Step 1 — Open Google Photos and sign in
Find the **Google Photos** app — its icon is a pinwheel in red, yellow, green, and blue — and tap it. If the app asks you to sign in, use your Google account (the one you use for Gmail or YouTube).
You'll know it worked when your photos appear in a grid.

💬 Example:
Open Google Photos → sign in with your Google account → wait for your photos to load.

---

## Step 2 — Make sure Face Groups is turned on
At the top, tap your **profile photo** or **initials**. Tap **Google Photos settings**, then **Privacy**, and turn **Face Groups** on. This is the setting that lets Google Photos group similar faces together.
You'll know it worked when the Face Groups switch shows as on.

💬 Example:
Profile photo → **Google Photos settings** → **Privacy** → **Face Groups**: on.

---

## Step 3 — Find the people in your photos
At the bottom of the screen, tap **Collections**, then **People & pets**. You'll see the face groups Google Photos has made — each one is a small round picture of a face. If you've only just turned Face Groups on, the groups may not be ready yet; come back to this screen a little later.
You'll know it worked when you see a row of faces under **People & pets**.

💬 Example:
Tap **Collections** → **People & pets** → look through the faces.

---

## Step 4 — Name the people you care about
Tap a face to open its group. At the top of the group, tap **Add a name**, then type a name or nickname — for example "Mom", "Liam", or "Grandpa Joe". Names only help you; they make the people easy to pick in the next step.
Sometimes Google Photos shows you two groups and asks whether they are the same person. Tap **Same**, **Different**, or **Not sure**. If you give a second group a name you've already used, Google Photos asks if you want to merge the two face groups.
You'll know it worked when the name appears under that face in **People & pets**.

💬 Example:
Tap a face → **Add a name** → type `Dad` → confirm.

---

## Step 5 — Create a live album that fills itself
Go back to the main screen. At the top right, tap **Add**, then **Album**. Tap **Select people & pets**. On each face group you want in the album — say Mom, Dad, and Liam — tap **Select**. At the top right, tap **Confirm**.
This is a **live album**: from now on, new photos of the people you picked are added to it automatically. You can give it a title such as "Family 2025".
You'll know it worked when the album opens and shows photos of the people you chose.

💬 Example:
**Add** → **Album** → **Select people & pets** → tap **Select** on Mom, Dad, and Liam → **Confirm**.

---

## Step 6 — Share the album with family
Open the album and tap **Share**. To get a link you can send anywhere, tap **Create link**. Paste it into a text message or an email. Google's help notes that anyone who has the link can view the album, so send it only to people you trust.
You'll know it worked when you have a link ready to paste.

💬 Example:
Open "Family 2025" → **Share** → **Create link** → paste the link into a message to Grandma.

---

## Step 7 — Let the album keep itself up to date
Because it's a live album, you don't need to add new photos by hand. Every few weeks, open **Collections** → **People & pets** and use **Add a name** on any new faces you care about, so they are easy to find and pick next time.
You'll know it worked when new photos of your family show up in the album without you adding them.

💬 Example:
Take a few new photos of your kids → open "Family 2025" a day later → check that they've appeared.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Mistake:** You can't find **People & pets**.
  **Fix:** Google lists three reasons: the feature isn't available in your region, Face Groups is turned off in settings (turn it on as in Step 2), or no face groups have been created yet (check back later).

- **Mistake:** A photo of someone else ended up in the album.
  **Fix:** Face Groups isn't perfect, and Google says so itself. Open the photo in the album and remove it from the album — it stays in your library.

- **Mistake:** The same person appears as two different faces.
  **Fix:** Give both groups the same name. Google Photos will ask whether you want to merge the face groups.

---

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:**
  No more scrolling through hundreds of photos to find pictures of your child's birthday or your last holiday. One album gathers every photo of your family and keeps growing on its own, ready to share with relatives.

- **For your business or work:**
  For team events or project photos, a shared album link beats a pile of email attachments. Only add people's faces to groups and albums with their permission.

- **If you're just getting started:**
  Name just one or two people first. Once you see the live album fill up, add the rest of the family.

---
## Try it now
Open Google Photos, tap **Collections** → **People & pets**, and use **Add a name** on one face. Then tap **Add** → **Album** → **Select people & pets** to make your first live album — it takes about two minutes.
